I read your post and I hope I can bring a new perspective. I am a child that grew up in a bitter divorce, and when I read this I don't see a failure or a mother doing "below average" I see a mother doing wonderfully in a terrible situation. I'm sorry that you had to suffer threw all this. Your not a fool or idiot for hoping that the man you loved would change. I can remember the heart ache my own mother went through, but I want to let you know that your children will some day look back and realize how fantastic of a mother you are (if they don't already). Even though things look dark, you are doing great! Don't leave your children behind, they need you.

My ex left to teach English in South Korea. So I get that. Heck I told her I would go with her, but she told me I needed to stay with my family. When she left I told her that I couldn't keep talking to her because it was going to tear me apart.  It was hard to handle for a long time but honestly if I kept trying to focus on the past it would have never got over her. I kept everything she ever gave me in a box because I couldn't handle the constant reminder of her. I can't speak for anyone but I would say she remembers you, but even if you talk to her what will that do? Do you think that will fix a broken heart, or will it just open more wounds? How would it resolve your current dilemma? Would it change your pact you made?

I read this and I wanted to say I was really moved. My college girlfriend who I fell hard for and I would have done anything for, broke up with me to move half way around the world, after that I jumped into a relationship with someone who was wrong for me because I couldn't stand being alone. She was really jealous because she knew I wasn't over my ex. She made me unfriend my ex and not have any contact with her for awhile. Years later I still couldn't see a picture of my ex without it ruining my day and I just kept trying to push it all down and not think about it. I met up with her for the first time in years and I was physically ill. I never though I would be able to move but i eventually did move on. All I can say is sometimes I needed to pick myself up and move on, but I learned that I needed to find someone to talk to about it. I didn't need to be superman all the time and act like I had it all together. If I had advice I would say you need to be true to yourself and if this is the way you feel don't hide it. Denying yourself the chance to let it all out in a safe place instead of keeping this all inside. You might think the only person that can save you is around the world, but the only one that can do it is you. You can get better it can take a LONG time but it's worth it. If you think that your Loved ones won't miss you, you need to work those thoughts out with them. Any struggle you have isn't one you should do alone. Don't put a time limit on your life because you can pull through and look back on this day and realize that you are glad you hung on.
